I read the whole file and checked its new definitions against Mathlib. The new definitions are `ConvergesToOne`, `ConvergingGenData`, `ConvergingGenData.Le`, `top`, `limit`, `reps`, `refineSet` and `refine`.

`ConvergesToOne s` is defined as `Tendsto ((↑) : s → G) cofinite (𝓝 1)`. Searching Mathlib for `cofinite (𝓝 1)` and "converges to one" found only the following. These are lemmas about maps `f : α → G` tending to 1 along the cofinite filter: `Multipliable.tendsto_cofinite_one`, `cauchySeq_prod_of_tendsto_cofinite_one`, and the nonarchimedean multipliable iff. Mathlib has no set-level predicate or competing definition. The file uses the Mathlib building blocks directly, for example `Filter.Tendsto`, `isCompact_insert_range_of_cofinite` and `Filter.Tendsto.convergesToOne_range`. It is also used in several other TauCeti files, so it is a deliberate named API.

`ConvergingGenData` and its `Le` relation are private, problem-specific structures for a Zorn argument. They have no Mathlib counterpart. The remaining declarations are theorems or use existing notions (`Group.rank`, `topologicalClosure`, `OpenNormalSubgroup`, `QuotientGroup.mk'`). I did not read `TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Generation.lean`, which holds `IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated`. The file here only uses that declaration and does not define it.
